name: GirlsWhoML & PhysicsX Hackathon
description:
If commercial space flights land on Mars tomorrow, what would you build to create the Martian city? 
 [APPLICATIONS CLOSED] 
 Join GirlsWhoML and PhysicsX for an evening hackathon in London to tackle the first human landing on Mars, supported by Cursor. You arrive on an empty, rust-red planet with no city, no roads, and no infrastructure. What do you build first? 
 You’ll design and prototype one core system for the Martian city, across three tracks: Architecture, Vehicles, and Life Support . Every build should combine engineering, machine learning, or 3D modelling. 
 The window is short, but that’s the point: see how far you can push what’s possible in a single evening. Mentors will be on the floor throughout, your work will be reviewed by a panel of industry judges, and every participant gets Cursor credits supported by Francisco Terpolilli, Cursor's EU Ambassador and Regional Leader. 
 Bring a team of 2-3, or turn up solo and we’ll help you find a crew, at our team formation session. Women, non-binary, and allies are all welcome. 
 Prizes provided by PhysicsX , including career coaching and mentorship opportunities, to be announced. 
 Bring your curiosity, your laptop, and your ambition. The city starts with you.

name: Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hackathon @ NYU
description:
📋 Event Description 
 Generative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, and candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, and TA practitioners who live this problem every week. 
 This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc , Integral Recruiting (IRD) , and NYU — where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge. 
 🎯 The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel 
 Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel — recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, and candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, and that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it. 
 You can attack either side of the funnel — or the seam between them. 
 Side A — Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, and a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike — the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments — a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, and the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet.

9:45 – 10:30 am | Session 1: From Testimony to Accountability: A UN Framework Protocol on CRSV

Moderator: Tatiana Kotlyarenko, Member of IF20 Advisory Group on Human Trafficking

Despite a robust body of international humanitarian, human rights and criminal law addressing conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV), a persistent gap remains between international commitments and their effective implementation at the national level. This high-level panel will examine the case for a United Nations Framework Protocol on the Implementation of International Obligations relating to Conflict-Related Sexual Violence and Survivor-Centred Responses, a practical framework designed not to create new legal obligations, but to help States translate existing commitments into effective prevention, reporting and documentation, national response frameworks, justice and accountability, comprehensive referral mechanisms, and long-term support for victims and survivors. Building on existing international standards and good practices, including the Murad Code, the discussion will consider how a Framework Protocol could strengthen survivor-centred and trauma-informed approaches, national coordination and international cooperation, while addressing emerging challenges and opportunities related to digital evidence, artificial intelligence and responsible innovation. The panel will bring together experts to identify priority implementation gaps and launch a global consultation process towards the development of the Framework Protocol.

name: Superpollutant Action Summit
description:
The Superpollutant Action Summit, convened by Beyond Alliance, is a first of its kind gathering for high-level leaders across business, science, government, and civil society to come together for a full day to accelerate action on the pollutants driving the most near-term warming: methane, black carbon, N₂O, and HFCs. 
 Rapid reductions over the next decade could meaningfully bend the warming curve before mid-century, making this one of the fastest and most immediate levers available for climate progress, with the added benefit of real air quality and health gains along the way. 
 Momentum on superpollutants has been building across governments, companies, and civil society, from the Global Methane Pledge to a wave of new corporate commitments like the Superpollutant Action Initiative, a $100 million effort from Amazon, Autodesk, Figma, Google, JPMorgan Chase, Salesforce, and Workday to fund high impact mitigation projects, coordinated by Beyond Alliance. 
 The event will bring together 150+ decision-makers driving climate action in business, finance, policy, and innovation. Through deep dives on corporate Scope 3 action, emerging market mechanisms, voluntary carbon markets, and the policies and financing needed to scale solutions, the day is built for candid dialogue and real commitments. 
 Across the day, expect candid actionable plenary conversations on where science, policy, and capital meet, thematic breakouts, a look at what it will take to finance faster action at scale, and a showcase of real solutions from the innovators and project developers building them.

name: Banking: From Boring to Climate Superpower
description:
We've been programmed to think of banking as a utility: boring by design. Simply a safe place to park our money. A decision with little consequence beyond the financial. 
 But nothing could be further from the truth. 
 Our everyday banking decisions generate massive emissions and fuel an invisible hand driving the climate crisis as well as social and environmental injustice around the world. In fact, research from Topo Finance found that, for many of the world's largest companies, the emissions generated by their cash and investments exceeded all their other emissions combined: their operations, their products, even their AI. 
 We have an opportunity to change that. By leveraging our financial management, we can drive positive impact and help transform the financial system into a visible hand for environmental and social progress around the world. 
 Join us for an exciting conversation about how corporations, municipalities, organisations and individuals are transforming their banking from one of their largest climate drivers into one of their greatest superpowers.

 Build systems that help agents preserve what matters and discard what doesn't, staying reliable as tasks stretch from minutes to hours, days, or longer.

name: Claude for Blockchain: Trading Agents
description:
Pre-TOKEN2049 edition · Claude Singapore Community 
 In March, OKX did something no major exchange had done: they open-sourced a toolkit that lets an AI agent trade directly on their platform. Spot, futures, options, grid bots — 80+ tools, MIT licensed, running locally on your machine. 
 Most of the industry still hasn't looked at it. 
 This session is a straight, practical hour on what exchange-native AI trading actually is, what it can and can't do, and what it means for how you work. 
 What we'll cover 
 What OKX actually shipped. The Agent Trade Kit, how it plugs into Claude Code through MCP, and the real scope of what an agent can reach — market data, order execution, position management, automated strategies. 
 The security model, honestly. Your API keys stay in a local config file. The model never sees them. Signing happens on your machine. Why that design matters, and where the remaining risk actually sits. 
 How people are using it. Research and market analysis, monitoring, strategy testing in demo mode, and execution. Where each one genuinely helps, and where it falls apart. 
 The part nobody wants to say out loud. AI makes mistakes, and you own the losses. What guardrails look like in practice — read-only mode, demo profiles, permission-scoped keys — and why you should never skip them. 
 Where the edge goes. When every desk can run the same agent on the same public data, what's actually left worth having. 
 Then we build one, live 
 Last fifteen minutes: a working agent wired to OKX through Claude Code, pulling live market data, running in read-only mode. From nothing to working, on stage. No laptops needed — just watch how little it takes.

name: TOKEN2049 Week Side Event, Singapore. 🇸🇬 Quantum Security for Digital Assets, Industry Leaders, Networking, Food & Beverages.
description:
Quantum Security for Digital Assets

This private technical event brings together industry leaders, protocol engineers, cryptography researchers, digital asset specialists and institutional stakeholders to examine the emerging security requirements of digital assets in a post quantum environment.

The discussion will focus on the cryptographic foundations required to protect digital asset infrastructure as quantum computing develops, including digital signatures, transaction authentication, identity, key management, consensus security and the protection of blockchain execution environments.

Panels with industry leaders will be followed by relaxed networking with senior peers over food and drinks.

Particular attention will be given to the transition from conventional elliptic curve cryptography toward post quantum cryptographic systems and the practical considerations involved in implementing these mechanisms at protocol level.

Topics will include

Post quantum digital signatures and transaction authentication

Quantum resistant identity and account structures

Key generation, address derivation and key lifecycle management

Post quantum consensus and validator communication

Cryptographic verification within distributed systems

Quantum resistant smart contract infrastructure

Migration considerations for existing digital asset systems

Security implications for institutional digital asset custody and infrastructure.

The discussion will also examine how post quantum cryptography can be integrated throughout a blockchain protocol rather than being implemented as an isolated security layer.

Quantova will present its approach to post quantum blockchain architecture, including the Quantova Virtual Machine and its implementation of PQR cryptographic primitives across transaction signing, account creation, consensus and execution.

Attendees will have the opportunity to examine the practical relationship between cryptographic primitives, protocol architecture and application execution, with discussion focused on implementation rather than commercial promotion.

About organizers:

Quantova runs a post-quantum Layer 1 network built from first principles to issue, move, settle and protect digital value: digital identity, stablecoins, tokenised real-world assets, payments and institutional settlement, without inheriting a future migration burden.

Quantova launched QDock.io, the development environment supporting post quantum application development, together with the underlying cryptographic libraries, compilation tooling and deployment infrastructure used within the Quantova environment.

Further technical information is available at Quantova.org

HackenProof is a bug bounty and crowdsourced security platform connecting companies with a global network of white-hat security researchers. The platform supports more than 400 programs, with over $26 million paid in bounties and a community of more than 85,000 ethical hackers.

Anna Tutova has been active in the digital asset industry for many years, working at the intersection of cryptocurrency regulation, institutional finance and quantum security. She has contributed to international regulatory and industry discussions and spoken at events across multiple regions, including on the evolving relationship between digital assets, regulation and post-quantum security.
